Approval and Adoption of the Minutes
Introduction of Artist - Joe Gohl
notes: Barb Lee, Arts Council introduced Joe Gohl as the artist currently displaying his art in the Council Chamber. Joe Gohl provided his career history and the sources of his inspiration.

items.title: Sarah Bowers-Peter Crime Stoppers Guelph Wellington
notes: Sarah Bowers-Peter indicated Crime Stoppers is celebrating their 35th anniversary. She noted Crime Stoppers is an anonymous, confidential method of reporting crime, there are cash rewards if arrests are made and they rely on fundraising and donations from individuals, businesses and organizations to pay rewards and operate the program.
She highlighted statistics such as total number of tips received 23,108, resulting arrests 1,596, cases cleared 2,307, charges laid 4,506 and the value of the property recovered $10,398,366.

items.title: County Council Report - Mary Lloyd, County Councillor Ward 5
notes: County Councillor Mary Lloyd highlighted the recent construction at Carroll Creek, ongoing activities at the various County Libraries, the successful Centre Wellington shuttle, the upcoming antique car show at the Wellington Museum, the new works garage in Arthur, and the new library in Erin. She noted the recent opening of Grace Gardens, transitional emergency housing, for the most vulnerable and responded to questions regarding the delivery of these services.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Mayor Watters acknowledged the volunteers currently serving on Heritage Centre Wellington for all their hard and dedicated work.

items.title: Land Acknowledgement Revision
notes: Report from K. Drexler, Manager of Community Development Presentation by Annie Veilleux, ASI

Annie Veilleux, ASI provided an overview of the updated report, noting after approval of the Land Acknowledgement in December 2022, additional feedback was received. She noted they have been working with the First Nations to address the comments received and have made updates accordingly.

In response to a question from Councillor Lustgarten-Evoy regarding use of the Land Acknowledgement, A. Veilleux indicated the Land Acknowledgement can be used when best suited, provided it is given in a meaningful and thoughtful way.

items.title: Procurement Policy
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer provided an overview of the report and responded to questions regarding efforts to streamline the procurement process and the inclusion of processes to encourage flexibility.

Councillor Adams indicated support for improving efficiency and removing barriers, but expressed a desire to maintain the signing authority of the Mayor and Clerk for contracts over $2 million and wished to put forward an amendment to that effect.

items.title: Demolition at Heritage Listed Properties 19 & 19A East Mill Street, Elora

Mariana Iglesias, Manager of Planning Services provided an overview of the report, outlining the staff and Heritage Centre Wellington recommendations for the properties at 19A East Mill Street and 19 East Mill Street.
Staff responded to questions regarding the future storage of the Monster Month supplies and the extent of the deterioration of the buildings.

motions.item_title: Demolition at Heritage Listed Properties 19 & 19A East Mill Street, Elora
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves the full demolition of the structure located at 19A East Mill Street, Elora, with the conditions set out in staff report PLN2023-42; AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington authorizes the removal of 19A East Mill Street, Elora, from the Municipal Heritage Register; AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington approves the partial demolition of the structure(s) located at 19 East Mill Street, Elora, specifically the 2 concrete block additions and steel clad shed, leaving the original stone structure to remain for future restoration, with the conditions set out in staff report PLN2023-42; AND THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington confirms that the property at 19 East Mill Street, Elora, shall remain on the Municipal Heritage Register.

motions.item_title: Notice of Reconsideration from Councillor MacDonald
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington reconsider and rescind its decision dated February 22, 2022, to reaffirm Alternative No. 3 – Remove Bridge Without Replacement as the preferred alternative for the Middlebrook Truss Bridge Municipal Class Environmental Assessment; AND THAT Council directs staff to work with the Township of Woolwich to facilitate the removal of the Middlebrook Truss Bridge superstructure while maintaining the existing bridge abutments and centre pier in-place for possible reuse at a later time as outlined in report No. IS2022-05.
